trickyParts: Only an object carrying a non-blank string fallback wraps visit, so the subtree record costs nothing on every other object; a wrapper installed for every object would cost one call per ancestor per piece on a deeply nested body and would have moved the measured bound.
A fallback that is not a string is no piece and must still be descended into: with fallback out of slackDisplayFields, slackWalkKeys puts such a key in the alphabetical tail like any other container.

The subtree record notes the strings the producer yields, not the ones take accepts, which is how the per-object tally already works, so a fallback equal to a line the message's own words suppressed is still dropped.
The committed claude-envoy plugin bundle mirrors skills/, and the required check-dist step fails if the skill file is edited without rebuilding it.
